st.ndtNote: Engine provided by M-Lab NDT7, the open measurement platform backed by Google · Single-connection academic measurement; loaded latency is the latency increase under load · Anonymous results feed M-Lab's public research dataset
st.ooklaSetupBody: This engine's hosted widget is being connected to Ookla Speedtest Custom and will be available here soon. Meanwhile, feel free to use the other engines.
st.ooklaNote: Test widget hosted by Ookla® Speedtest · Results can't be sent back automatically — enter them manually under “Test History” below to compare
st.ooklaSlowBody: The connection from your network may be unstable. Refresh the page and try again, or open Speedtest directly.
st.cfNote: Test traffic goes through Cloudflare's global edge nodes · The test transfers real data — mind your data cap on mobile · Results are saved only in your browser
st.slowTitle: The test widget is loading slowly
st.slowBody: The connection from your network to the test node may be unstable. Refresh the page and try again, or open the test engine directly.
st.ostNote: Test engine provided by OpenSpeedTest™ (MIT open source) · This engine can't send results back automatically — enter them manually under “Test History” below to compare
st.noscript: With JavaScript disabled you can still switch to the OpenSpeedTest engine, but theme switching and test history won't work.
hero.h1: Your internet speed, known in one test
hero.sub: Professional online speed testing: download, upload and latency in one click. Multiple test engines (Cloudflare edge nodes × OpenSpeedTest™ × M-Lab NDT7 × Ookla) cross-validate each other; everything runs locally in your browser, on phones, desktops and TVs alike.
interp.title: What do these numbers actually mean?
interp.sub: Different activities demand very different speeds. Use the reference tables below to quickly place your connection.
interp.downP: Streaming, downloads and browsing all rely on it — the metric most people care about.
interp.downR2: Fine for everyday use, easy 4K streaming
interp.downR4: Enthusiast grade. Huge files in seconds
interp.upP: The quality ceiling for video calls, live streaming and cloud backups. Home broadband is usually slower up than down.
interp.upR1: Light uploads only, call quality limited
interp.upR2: Enough for daily use, smooth HD streaming
interp.pingP: The round-trip time of a single packet — it decides how “responsive” games and calls feel.
interp.pingR2: Great. Smooth for mainstream online games
hist.title: Test History
hist.sub: Records are stored only in your browser (localStorage) and never uploaded to any server.
hist.tip: Tip: after a test you can also enter results manually to compare multiple runs.
hist.empty: No records yet. Go run a test first.
